ops.title: launchd.Remove boots out without waiting for the process to exit
ops.description:
removeWhen (launchd/apply.go:180-202) runs launchctl bootout and then deletes the plist
in the very next statement:

	if bootout := c.launchctl(ctx, "bootout", serviceTarget(label)); !bootout.settled() {
		return fmt.Errorf("launchd: remove agent %q: %w", label, bootout.fail())
	}
	if err := durable.Remove(path); err != nil {

Nothing between those two lines observes the process. settled()
(launchd/launchctl.go:98-100) classifies launchctl's own exit status and nothing else —
it answers true for launchctlLoaded or launchctlNotLoaded — and launchctl bootout returns
once teardown is INITIATED, not once the process has exited. So Remove's postcondition is
"launchd accepted the bootout", not "the job is gone", while its name and its use say the
latter.

The composed public paths are correctly ordered and do wait. Client.Stop loops stopOnce to
a proof of departure and only then calls removeAgent (stop.go:77-96), which is exactly what
its doc comment promises: "The LaunchAgent goes last, after departure is proven, so launchd
never relaunches what was just drained" (stop.go:41-43). deploy takes RuntimeProof from
Quiesce (deploy/quiesce.go:90, called at deploy/deploy.go:470) before it converges. The gap
is launchd.Remove (launchd/apply.go:103) and RemoveUnmarked (:126) called directly: they are
exported, they have no wait, and nothing guards a caller against assuming the process is
gone when they return. A caller that boots out and then deletes the job's state directory
races the still-writing process.

Seen in the field as cc-pool bug 7648cd1 (rm -rf of the runtime state dir failing with
"Directory not empty" straight after a successful bootout). There the operator was driving
raw launchctl, not this function, so that incident is not evidence against daemonkit — but
it is exactly the shape a direct launchd.Remove caller would hit.

Note that TestRemoveBootsOutAndDeletesTheMarkedLabel (launchd/apply_test.go:373-389)
currently encodes the no-wait behaviour as correct: it drives a synchronous recorder and
asserts the verb list is exactly []string{"bootout"} with the plist already gone. Any fix
must keep that test satisfiable — a wait that observes an already-departed job has to cost
zero extra launchctl verbs.

ops.text: launchd.Remove does not delete the plist until the job's process has actually left the process table, not merely until launchctl bootout has returned.
A test proves the wait: a Runner whose bootout returns while the job is still live makes Remove wait (or fail on expiry) instead of deleting the plist immediately.
TestRemoveBootsOutAndDeletesTheMarkedLabel (launchd/apply_test.go:373-389) still passes — a synchronous mock whose job is already gone must still see exactly one bootout verb and a deleted plist.
